title: Jordan Algebras, Spin Factors, and Alternative Examples

items.title: Jordan algebra over a field of characteristic not two

references.title: N. Jacobson, Lectures on Quadratic Jordan Algebras, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, 1969
John C. Baez, The Octonions, arXiv:math/0105155v4 (2002)

items.definition: Let $k$ be a field with $operatorname{char}(k)\ne2$ ([[def-field]]) and let $J$ be a $k$-vector space ([[def-vector-space]]). A **Jordan $k$-algebra** is a bilinear product $\circ:J\times J\to J$ (linear in each argument) such that $x\circ y=y\circ x$ and $x\circ(y\circ x^2)=(x\circ y)\circ x^2$ for all $x,y\in J$, where $x^2:=x\circ x$. Associativity is not required. It is **unital** if there is $1_J\in J$ with $1_J\circ x=x$ for all $x$.

items.title: Alternative algebra

references.title: N. Jacobson, Lectures on Quadratic Jordan Algebras, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, 1969
Holger P. Petersson, Albert Algebras, Fields Institute lecture notes (2012)

items.definition: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a $k$-vector space. An **alternative $k$-algebra** is a bilinear product $A\times A\to A$ (linear in each argument) satisfying $x(xy)=(x^2)y$ and $(yx)x=y(x^2)$ for all $x,y\in A$, where $x^2:=xx$. Associativity and a unit are not part of this definition.

items.title: Complex associative algebra with involution

references.title: N. Jacobson, Lectures on Quadratic Jordan Algebras, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, 1969
Holger P. Petersson, Albert Algebras, Fields Institute lecture notes (2012)

items.definition: A **complex associative algebra with involution** is a unital associative algebra over $\mathbb C$ ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) equipped with a conjugate-linear map $a\mapsto a^*$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]) such that $(a^*)^*=a$, $(ab)^*=b^*a^*$, and $1^*=1$. The self-adjoint part is $A_{\rm sa}:=\{a\in A:a^*=a\}$, regarded as a real vector space.

items.title: Symmetrized product of an associative algebra

references.title: N. Jacobson, Lectures on Quadratic Jordan Algebras, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, 1969
John C. Baez, The Octonions, arXiv:math/0105155v4 (2002)

items.definition: Let $k$ be a field with $\operatorname{char}(k)\ne2$ and $A$ a unital associative $k$-algebra as in [[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]] (its multiplication is $k$-bilinear). On the underlying $k$-vector space define $a\circ b:=\frac12(ab+ba)$. Denote this algebra-with-product by $A^+$. This definition makes no associativity claim for $\circ$ and does not by itself assert the Jordan identity.

items.title: The symmetrized product of an associative algebra is Jordan

references.title: N. Jacobson, Lectures on Quadratic Jordan Algebras, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, 1969
John C. Baez, The Octonions, arXiv:math/0105155v4 (2002)

items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic not $2$ and $A$ a unital associative $k$-algebra. Then $A^+$ from [[def-associative-jordan-product]] is a Jordan algebra. If $A$ is a complex associative algebra with involution as in [[def-involutive-complex-associative-algebra]], then $A_{\rm sa}$ is closed under $\circ$ and is a real Jordan subalgebra of $A^+

items.title: Real spin-factor product

references.title: John C. Baez, The Octonions, arXiv:math/0105155v4 (2002)
N. Jacobson, Lectures on Quadratic Jordan Algebras, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, 1969

items.definition:
Let $(V,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$ be a real inner-product space with the convention in [[def-inner-product-space]] (over $\mathbb R$ the inner product is symmetric positive definite). On $S(V):=V\oplus\mathbb R$ define

$$
(v,\alpha)\circ(w,\beta):=(\alpha w+\beta v,\langle v,w\rangle+\alpha\beta).
$$

The pair $(S(V),\circ)$ is the real spin-factor product; its unit and Jordan identity are established in [[thm-real-spin-factor-is-jordan]].

items.title: The real spin factor satisfies the Jordan identity

references.title: John C. Baez, The Octonions, arXiv:math/0105155v4 (2002)
N. Jacobson, Lectures on Quadratic Jordan Algebras, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, 1969

items.statement: For every real inner-product space $V$, the product on $S(V)$ in [[def-real-spin-factor]] is commutative and bilinear, has unit $(0,1)$, and satisfies $x\circ(y\circ x^2)=(x\circ y)\circ x^2$. Hence it is a unital real Jordan algebra.

items.title: The spin factor and the plus-quadratic Clifford convention

references.title: John C. Baez, The Octonions, arXiv:math/0105155v4 (2002)
N. Jacobson, Lectures on Quadratic Jordan Algebras, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, 1969

items.statement: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, let $Q(v)=\langle v,v\rangle$, and use the plus-$Q$ Clifford algebra $\mathrm{Cl}^{+}(V,Q)$ of [[def-clifford-algebra-of-a-quadratic-space]]. The map $\Phi:S(V)\to \mathrm{Cl}^{+}(V,Q)^+$, $\Phi(v,\alpha)=\bar v+\alpha 1$ is an injective unital Jordan homomorphism onto the Jordan subalgebra $\mathbb R1+\bar V$. In particular, $\bar v\bar w+\bar w\bar v=2\langle v,w\rangle1$. The spin-factor square cone is exactly $\{(v,\alpha):\alpha\geq\|v\|\}$, whose boundary is the future null cone $\{(v,\alpha):\alpha\geq0,\ \alpha^2-\|v\|^2=0\}$ of $q(v,\alpha)=\alpha^2-\|v\|^2$.

items.title: Real octonions by Cayley–Dickson doubling

references.title: N. Jacobson, Lectures on Quadratic Jordan Algebras, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, 1969
Holger P. Petersson, Albert Algebras, Fields Institute lecture notes (2012)
John C. Baez, The Octonions, arXiv:math/0105155v4 (2002)

items.definition:
As a real vector space set $\mathbb O:=\mathbb H\times\mathbb H$, with componentwise addition and real scalar multiplication, using the quaternion algebra and conjugation of [[def-quaternions]]. Define

$$
(a,b)(c,d):=(ac-\bar d\,b,\; da+b\bar c),\qquad \overline{(a,b)}:=(\bar a,-b).
$$

The unit is $(1,0)$, and $i=(i,0)$, $j=(j,0)$, $k=(k,0)$, $\ell=(0,1)$, with $i\ell=(0,i)$, $j\ell=(0,j)$, and $k\ell=(0,k)$. This fixes the multiplication convention; the alternative laws and nonassociativity are proved in [[thm-octonions-are-alternative-but-not-associative]].

items.title: Quaternion conjugation is an anti-involution

references.title: N. Jacobson, Lectures on Quadratic Jordan Algebras, §8
John C. Baez, The Octonions, arXiv:math/0105155v4
Holger P. Petersson, Albert Algebras, §3

items.statement: For the quaternion algebra $\mathbb H$ of [[def-quaternions]], conjugation satisfies $\bar{\bar a}=a$, $a+\bar a=\widehat{2a_0}$ for $a=(a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3)$, and $\overline{ab}=\bar b\,\bar a$ for all $a,b\in\mathbb H.

items.title: Octonion conjugation is an anti-involution

references.title: N. Jacobson, Lectures on Quadratic Jordan Algebras, §8
John C. Baez, The Octonions, arXiv:math/0105155v4
Holger P. Petersson, Albert Algebras, §3

items.statement: For $\mathbb O$ of [[def-octonion-algebra-by-cayley-dickson]], conjugation satisfies $\overline{\bar x}=x$ and $\overline{xy}=\bar y\bar x$. If $x=(a,b)$ with $a,b\in\mathbb H$, then $x+\bar x=(\widehat{2a_0},0)$ and $x\bar x=\bar x x=(\widehat{N(a)+N(b)},0)$, a real scalar.

items.title: The Cayley–Dickson octonions are alternative but not associative

references.title: N. Jacobson, Lectures on Quadratic Jordan Algebras, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, 1969
Holger P. Petersson, Albert Algebras, Fields Institute lecture notes (2012)
John C. Baez, The Octonions, arXiv:math/0105155v4 (2002)

items.statement: For $\mathbb O$ as in [[def-octonion-algebra-by-cayley-dickson]], both alternative laws $x(xy)=x^2y$ and $(yx)x=yx^2$ hold. Multiplication is not associative: with the named basis elements, $(ij)\ell=k\ell$ while $i(j\ell)=-k\ell$. Thus $\mathbb O$ is an alternative nonassociative real algebra.

items.title: Hermitian three-by-three octonion matrix data

references.title: N. Jacobson, Lectures on Quadratic Jordan Algebras, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, 1969
Holger P. Petersson, Albert Algebras, Fields Institute lecture notes (2012)
John C. Baez, The Octonions, arXiv:math/0105155v4 (2002)

items.definition:
Let

$$
H_3(\mathbb O):=\left\{\begin{pmatrix}a&x&\bar z\\\bar x&b&y\\z&\bar y&c\end{pmatrix}:a,b,c\in\mathbb R,\ x,y,z\in\mathbb O\right\}.
$$

For octonion matrices define $(XY)_{ij}:=\sum_{r=1}^3 X_{ir}Y_{rj}$ with each product in the displayed order. The ambient symmetrized matrix expression is $m(X,Y):=\frac12(XY+YX)\in M_3(\mathbb O)$. Closure of this expression in $H_3(\mathbb O)$ and its Jordan identity are established in [[thm-real-albert-algebra-is-jordan]]; no claim is made for other matrix sizes.

items.title: The real Albert algebra is a Jordan algebra

references.title: N. Jacobson, Lectures on Quadratic Jordan Algebras, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, 1969
Holger P. Petersson, Albert Algebras, Fields Institute lecture notes (2012)
John C. Baez, The Octonions, arXiv:math/0105155v4 (2002)

items.statement: For real octonions $\mathbb O$ with the multiplication in [[def-octonion-algebra-by-cayley-dickson]], the expression $X\circ Y:=\frac12(XY+YX)$ maps $H_3(\mathbb O)\times H_3(\mathbb O)$ into $H_3(\mathbb O)$ and makes it a unital real Jordan algebra. This is the real Albert algebra in this matrix realization; no classification or assertion for $H_n(\mathbb O)$ with $n\ne3$ is included.

title: Jordan Algebras, Spin Factors, and Alternative Examples: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: The symmetrized product need not be associative

references.title: N. Jacobson, Lectures on Quadratic Jordan Algebras, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, 1969
John C. Baez, The Octonions, arXiv:math/0105155v4 (2002)

items.statement: The false statement is: the product of every Jordan algebra is associative. The counterexample is the real Jordan algebra of symmetric $2\times2$ matrices with $P\circ Q=(PQ+QP)/2

items.title: The self-adjoint part need not be an associative subalgebra

references.title: N. Jacobson, Lectures on Quadratic Jordan Algebras, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, 1969
John C. Baez, The Octonions, arXiv:math/0105155v4 (2002)

items.statement: The false statement is: the self-adjoint part of every complex associative algebra with involution is closed under the original associative multiplication. The counterexample is $M_2(\mathbb C)$ with conjugate transpose.

items.title: The spin factor on the real plane

references.title: John C. Baez, The Octonions, arXiv:math/0105155v4 (2002)
N. Jacobson, Lectures on Quadratic Jordan Algebras, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, 1969

items.statement: For $V=\mathbb R^2$ with its standard inner product, the spin factor has unit $(0,1)$, and for $v=(x,y)$ its square is $(2\alpha v,x^2+y^2+\alpha^2)$. Its square cone is $\alpha\ge\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$, with Lorentz boundary $\alpha^2=x^2+y^2$.

items.title: A concrete octonion associator witness

references.title: N. Jacobson, Lectures on Quadratic Jordan Algebras, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, 1969
Holger P. Petersson, Albert Algebras, Fields Institute lecture notes (2012)

items.statement: With $i=(i,0)$, $j=(j,0)$, $k=(k,0)$, and $\ell=(0,1)$ in the Cayley–Dickson model, $(ij)\ell=k\ell$ but $i(j\ell)=-k\ell\ne k\ell$. The same product is alternative by the A-page theorem.

items.title: An off-diagonal product in the Albert algebra
